question.text: What causes most Texas crashes, and what information do drivers exchange after one?

answer.text: Most Texas crashes trace to speeding, botched yielding or stopping, and alcohol impairment, and crash drivers trade names, addresses, phones, vehicle numbers, plate numbers, license facts, and insurance facts when asked and available, copying insurer names and policy numbers verbatim while insurer gaps go to the insurance department hotline, plus crash locations and witness contacts.

teaching.text: Speeding, yielding or stopping errors, and alcohol cause most Texas crashes, and drivers exchange names, plates, license, and insurance details. Remember: names, plates, insurance.

question.text: What are the top crash causes, and how should insurance details be copied?

answer.text: Top causes run speeding, bad yielding, and drink, while exchanges run names through insurance with verbatim policy copies.

teaching.text: The top causes are speed, yielding or stopping, and alcohol, and insurance details are copied exactly. Remember: copy policy numbers exactly.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Top causes run speeding, bad yielding, and drink, while exchanges run names through insurance with verbatim policy copies.

question.text: When must law enforcement be told about a crash immediately?

answer.text: Law enforcement hears immediately about injuries or deaths, immovable vehicles, fleeing drivers, and suspected intoxication.

teaching.text: Call law enforcement immediately for an injury or death, an immovable vehicle, a fleeing driver, or suspected intoxication. Remember: injury, stuck car, fleeing, drunk.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Law enforcement hears immediately about injuries or deaths, immovable vehicles, fleeing drivers, and suspected intoxication.

question.text: Which crashes need a written report, and how soon?

answer.text: Uninvestigated crashes without injury, death, or one thousand dollars of property damage need a written transportation-department report on its form within ten days of the crash.

teaching.text: A crash police do not investigate, with no injury or death and under one thousand dollars of damage, needs a written report within ten days. Remember: written report, ten days.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Uninvestigated crashes without injury, death, or one thousand dollars of property damage need a written transportation-department report on its form within ten days of the crash.

question.text: How do immediate police calls differ from the ten-day written report?

answer.text: Four triggers summon police at once, while minor uninvestigated crashes file written reports within ten days under one thousand dollars.

teaching.text: Four triggers mean call now; a minor uninvestigated crash means a written report within ten days. Remember: call now or file later.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Four triggers summon police at once, while minor uninvestigated crashes file written reports within ten days under one thousand dollars.

question.text: What must a driver do after a crash with injury or death?

answer.text: Injury-or-death crashes demand immediate stops at or near scenes without needless obstruction plus immediate returns and stays, handing name, address, registration, and insurer to injured parties and vehicle attendants, flashing licenses when asked and available, and rendering reasonable aid including doctor-or-hospital transport when needed or requested.

teaching.text: After an injury or death crash, stop, return and stay, give your name, address, registration, and insurer, and render reasonable aid. Remember: stop, identify, render aid.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Injury-or-death crashes demand immediate stops at or near scenes without needless obstruction plus immediate returns and stays, handing name, address, registration, and insurer to injured parties and vehicle attendants, flashing licenses when asked and available, and rendering reasonable aid including doctor-or-hospital transport when needed or requested.

question.text: What must a driver do after a crash that damages only vehicles?

answer.text: Vehicle-damage-only crashes with driven or attended cars demand immediate near-scene stops, prompt moves to investigation sites, frontage roads, cross streets, or suitable spots when main-lane cars stay drivable, immediate returns and stays, and the same name, address, registration, insurer, and on-request license handoffs.

teaching.text: After a vehicle-only crash, stop, move drivable main-lane cars to a suitable spot, and give the same information. Remember: stop, move clear, identify.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Vehicle-damage-only crashes with driven or attended cars demand immediate near-scene stops, prompt moves to investigation sites, frontage roads, cross streets, or suitable spots when main-lane cars stay drivable, immediate returns and stays, and the same name, address, registration, insurer, and on-request license handoffs.

question.text: How do the duties after an injury crash differ from a vehicle-only crash?

answer.text: Injury crashes stop, identify, and aid, while vehicle-only crashes stop, move drivable cars clear, and identify.

teaching.text: Injury crashes add rendering aid; vehicle-only crashes add moving drivable cars clear. Remember: aid versus move clear.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Injury crashes stop, identify, and aid, while vehicle-only crashes stop, move drivable cars clear, and identify.

question.text: What are the penalties for fleeing a crash with injury or death?

answer.text: Fleeing injury-or-death crashes punishes death as second-degree felony up to ten thousand dollars with two to twenty TDCJ years, serious bodily injury as third-degree felony up to ten thousand dollars with two to ten years, and plain injury with up to five TDCJ years or one county year and up to five thousand dollars.

teaching.text: Fleeing a death crash is a second-degree felony, serious injury a third-degree felony, and plain injury brings prison or jail and a fine. Remember: fleeing death: felony.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Fleeing injury-or-death crashes punishes death as second-degree felony up to ten thousand dollars with two to twenty TDCJ years, serious bodily injury as third-degree felony up to ten thousand dollars with two to ten years, and plain injury with up to five TDCJ years or one county year and up to five thousand dollars.

question.text: How do fleeing penalties change for death, serious injury, and plain injury?

answer.text: Fleeing death draws second-degree felony years, serious injury draws third-degree felony years, and plain injury draws prison or jail plus fines.

teaching.text: Match the harm to the step: death second-degree, serious injury third-degree, plain injury prison or jail. Remember: death, serious, plain injury.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Fleeing death draws second-degree felony years, serious injury draws third-degree felony years, and plain injury draws prison or jail plus fines.

question.text: What are the penalties for fleeing a crash that damages only vehicles?

answer.text: Fleeing vehicle-damage crashes costs Class C up to five hundred dollars under two hundred dollars of damage, or Class B up to two thousand dollars and one hundred eighty jailed days at two hundred dollars or more.

teaching.text: Fleeing a vehicle-damage crash is Class C under two hundred dollars of damage and Class B with jail at two hundred or more. Remember: two hundred dollar line.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Fleeing vehicle-damage crashes costs Class C up to five hundred dollars under two hundred dollars of damage, or Class B up to two thousand dollars and one hundred eighty jailed days at two hundred dollars or more.

question.text: Where does the penalty for fleeing a property-only crash split?

answer.text: Property-only fleeing splits at two hundred dollars, Class C below and Class B with jail above.

teaching.text: Two hundred dollars of damage is the line between Class C and Class B. Remember: below Class C, above Class B.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Property-only fleeing splits at two hundred dollars, Class C below and Class B with jail above.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: below Class C, above Class B

question.text: What must you do after striking an unattended vehicle?

answer.text: Unattended-vehicle strikes demand immediate stops with owner searches and name-and-address handoffs, or visible written notices carrying names, addresses, and crash circumstances, under the same under-two-hundred Class C and two-hundred-plus Class B ladder.

teaching.text: After hitting an unattended car, find the owner or leave a visible note with your name, address, and what happened. Remember: find owner or leave note.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Unattended-vehicle strikes demand immediate stops with owner searches and name-and-address handoffs, or visible written notices carrying names, addresses, and crash circumstances, under the same under-two-hundred Class C and two-hundred-plus Class B ladder.

question.text: What must you do after striking a fixture, landscaping, or a structure?

answer.text: Fixture, landscaping, and structure strikes demand reasonable owner searches with crash notice, name, address, and registration handoffs, on-request license shows, ten-day written transportation reports for uninvestigated crashes under one thousand dollars to any one person without injury or death, and the same Class C and Class B fleeing ladder.

teaching.text: After hitting a fixture or structure, search for the owner, give notice and your registration, and file a ten-day report when required. Remember: find owner, give notice.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Fixture, landscaping, and structure strikes demand reasonable owner searches with crash notice, name, address, and registration handoffs, on-request license shows, ten-day written transportation reports for uninvestigated crashes under one thousand dollars to any one person without injury or death, and the same Class C and Class B fleeing ladder.

question.text: How do the duties after striking an unattended car differ from striking a fixture?

answer.text: Unattended cars get found owners or visible notes, while fixtures get found owners, notice, and possible ten-day reports.

teaching.text: Unattended cars get an owner or a visible note; fixtures get an owner search, notice, and possibly a report. Remember: note for cars, notice fixtures.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Unattended cars get found owners or visible notes, while fixtures get found owners, notice, and possible ten-day reports.

question.text: Why should hit-and-run victims report, and how should you help an injured person?

answer.text: Hit-and-run victims report crashes for investigation since uninsured motorist coverage pays reported cases, and helpers state locations clearly, summon skilled aid without trusting denials of injury, avoid moving victims or preserve positions when moves prove essential, stanch serious bleeding with clean thick pressure pads, and shelter victims from heat or cold.

teaching.text: Hit-and-run victims report for coverage, and helpers call skilled aid, avoid moving victims, stop bleeding with pads, and give shelter. Remember: report, call help, keep still.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Hit-and-run victims report crashes for investigation since uninsured motorist coverage pays reported cases, and helpers state locations clearly, summon skilled aid without trusting denials of injury, avoid moving victims or preserve positions when moves prove essential, stanch serious bleeding with clean thick pressure pads, and shelter victims from heat or cold.

question.text: What do hit-and-run victims and injured people each need?

answer.text: Hit-and-runs need police reports for coverage, and injured victims need clear locations, skilled help, stillness, pressure pads, and shelter.

teaching.text: Report the hit-and-run, and help the injured with a clear location, skilled aid, stillness, pressure, and shelter. Remember: report and gentle aid.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Hit-and-runs need police reports for coverage, and injured victims need clear locations, skilled help, stillness, pressure pads, and shelter.
